history.period: 1596 CE (traditional founding); present structure ~150 years old
history.summary: Major Shiva shrine at Basukinath town, Jarmundi block, Dumka district, Jharkhand, on the Deoghar-Dumka highway. It houses a swayambhu shivlinga traditionally dated to 1596; the present white-marble complex with its lotus-shaped dome is said to have been built by a tribal named Basaki (Baski) Tatme and renovated around 1810 by Queen Baidyanathi of Chota Nagpur (verify). Legend links the name to Vasuki, the serpent-king who worshipped the linga after Sagar Manthan, and to a farmer named Basu who found the linga. It is the 'court' (kachari/diwani) of Baba Baidyanath: pilgrims completing the Baidyanath Kanwar pilgrimage at Deoghar must also offer water here — 'Devghar ka kachari, Basukinath ka diwani'. The complex holds 30+ shrines and the Van Ganga/Shivaganga bathing pond; the Shiva and Parvati shrines face each other and their doors are not opened simultaneously. Note: seq 1604 (Parvati Temple, Basukinath) is the Parvati shrine within THIS complex — related/same-complex record, not a fully independent temple.

name: Basukinath Temple (Baba Basukinath Dham)
town_description: Basukinath is a pilgrimage town in the Jarmundi block of Dumka district, Jharkhand, on the Deoghar-Dumka state highway. It exists essentially around the Baba Basukinath Dham temple complex and swells with Kanwariya pilgrims during Shravan. The Santhal Pargana region around it is one of Jharkhand's most important Hindu pilgrimage corridors, paired with Deoghar's Baidyanath Dham.

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport, ~50 km (verify); Dumka has no commercial airport
travel.railway: Deoghar Junction, ~45 km (verify); local Basukinath Halt nearby (verify)
travel.road: On the Deoghar-Dumka state highway, ~45 km from Deoghar and ~25 km north-west of Dumka; buses, taxis and Kanwar routes

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan (July-August) for the Kanwar mela (very crowded)
